evidence.text: The database interprets the oracle graph as a facial outline enclosing an eye and gives ‘face’ as its original sense. It reports that 面 itself is not found in bronze inscriptions, though a related bronze graph uses 𦣻 with an enclosure. It describes a Chu-slip enclosure as altered toward 臼 and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are the database’s analyses and cited examples; I did not inspect the artifacts independently.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen form 麪, glossed 麥末也 (Duan Yucai’s text has 麥屑末也), and analyzes it as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic. It describes 麵 as a later common writing and notes that 玉篇 and 廣韻 equate 麵 with 麪. Its cited examples include flour/powder in 後漢書 and food uses in 南史 and Tang poetry; these citations do not independently date first attestations.

search_audit.outcome: Search found official Taiwanese Ministry entries, CUHK dictionary entries and the exact Commons redraw page. Opened the 面 paleographic record, both Ministry entries, the 麵 record and Commons page. Unihan pages and the Commons imageinfo API/direct SVG request returned internal errors. Local exact reading rows were separately inspected; those rows are not external-source verification.

gaps: No individually dated oracle inscription for 面 was inspected. The face depiction is the CUHK database’s modern analysis; the Shuowen explanation is historical lexicography, not independent confirmation of the earliest form.
CUHK reports 面 itself is unattested in bronze inscriptions, but the surveyed corpus and coverage limits are unspecified.

The cited Chu-slip form change toward 臼 and the face-toward example are reported by CUHK; the artifact and text were not independently inspected. Dates and semantic links for surface, side and dimension remain unresolved.

The dictionary sources distinguish flour from noodle/food examples, but their citations do not establish the earliest attestation of either sense. They also do not establish that the food word was borrowed from the face word 面.

麪 is explicitly analyzed with 丏 as phonetic; 面 in later 麵 is described as a sound-bearing element. No same-system local Baxter–Sagart reading for 麵 was found, so no reconstruction comparison between 面 and 麵 is offered. Neither the sound match nor the food word’s origin is proven merely by modern Mandarin miàn.
Official Unihan pages for U+9762 and U+9EB5 could not be accessed. The local exact rows show miàn, but external click-through verification was unavailable.

Commons’ page supplies the redraw’s stated identity, provenance references and public-domain terms, but the direct SVG and imageinfo API could not be opened for pixel inspection. No claim is made that the redraw was visually checked against an artifact.
No reuse terms were checked for the repeatedly cited text datasets; no local text extract is recommended.
